title: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Requirements & Process
metaDescription: Australia skilled worker visa 2026: subclass 189, 190 and 491 requirements, 65 points, skills assessment, TSMIT and application steps. Learn more.
headline: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Requirements & Process

sections.title: Skilled Worker Visa Pathways
sections.content:
Australia offers three main skilled worker pathways: subclass 189 for independent permanent residence, subclass 190 for state-nominated permanent residence, and subclass 491 for regional provisional residence. All run through SkillSelect, where applicants submit an Expression of Interest and receive invitations based on points. For 2026-27, Australia has allocated 21,090 places for the 189 and 35,500 for the 190.

Applicants must have an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, a positive skills assessment, and at least 65 points. In practice, invitations usually require higher scores because competition is strong. The 189 grants permanent residence immediately, while the 491 is a five-year provisional visa leading to permanent residence.

sections.title: The Points Test Explained
sections.content:
Points are awarded for age, qualifications, work experience, English ability and other factors. Applicants aged 25 to 32 receive maximum age points, a bachelor's degree earns 15 points, and superior English earns 20 points. Australian study and work experience add further points, and state nomination adds 5 points for the 190 or 15 for the 491.

Applicants must be under 45 and meet English, health and character requirements. If your occupation is not on the relevant list, you cannot proceed through SkillSelect. Checking the occupation list before investing in assessments and tests saves time and money.

sections.title: Skills Assessment and English Tests
sections.content:
Every applicant needs a skills assessment from the assessing body for their occupation. IT professionals are assessed by the Australian Computer Society, engineers by Engineers Australia, and trades workers by Trades Recognition Australia. The assessment confirms qualifications and experience meet Australian standards.

Accepted English tests include IELTS, PTE and TOEFL. Competent English is the minimum, but higher scores earn more points and are usually needed for a competitive total. For Singapore-based applicants, test centres in Singapore offer all major English tests with frequent sessions.

sections.title: Employer Sponsorship and TSMIT
sections.content:
Employer-sponsored options such as subclass 482 complement the points-tested visas. Under the 482, sponsors must pay at least the Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold of AUD 73,150 per year, and the offer must match the annual market salary rate for equivalent Australian workers in the same city. United States citizens benefit from an exemption from labour market testing under the Australia-US Free Trade Agreement.

Singapore citizens do not receive that particular exemption, but Singapore's strong trade relationship with Australia and the many Australian employers with Singapore operations make employer sponsorship a realistic route. After receiving an invitation, applicants have 60 days to lodge, and processing usually takes 6 to 18 months.

faqs.q: What score do I need for an Australian skilled worker visa?
faqs.a: You need at least 65 points to lodge an Expression of Interest, but invitations usually go to applicants with higher scores because places are limited. Points come from age, qualifications, work experience, English ability and other factors. State nomination adds 5 points for the 190 or 15 points for the 491,

faqs.q: What is the TSMIT for employer-sponsored visas?
faqs.a: The Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold is AUD 73,150 per year. Employers sponsoring workers under subclass 482 must pay at least this amount, and the salary must also match the annual market salary rate for equivalent Australian workers in the same location.

faqs.q: How long does the Australian skilled worker visa take?
faqs.a: Processing usually takes 6 to 18 months, depending on the subclass and the complexity of the case. After receiving an invitation through SkillSelect, you have 60 days to lodge a complete application. Having health and character documents ready at lodgement generally speeds up the process. The visa fee for subclass 189 is AUD 6,135 for the main applicant.

faqs.q: Can Singaporeans apply for Australian skilled worker visas?
faqs.a: Yes, Singapore citizens can apply through the same SkillSelect system as other nationalities. The main requirements are an occupation on the skilled list, a positive skills assessment, at least 65 points, and competent English. Singapore has many Australian employers with local operations, which also makes employer-sponsored subclass 482 visas a realistic alternative route to working in Australia.
